extracted.intended_audience: TV industry professionals and entertainment-news readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance/indicators implicit in Deadline's report about which comedy pilots MTV is ordering — what kinds of premises, talent, tones and market fits the network is prioritizing for scripted and unscripted half-hour comedy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: female-centered programming
rubrics_metrics.description: MTV is strengthening its focus on female viewers with Ladylike ... and three scripted pilot orders. Under Susanne Daniels, MTV moved away from male-centered comedy series ... to female-centered shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames a deliberate network strategy to favor female-driven shows and characters — projects that clearly target female viewers or center on women's perspectives (e.g., Girl Code alumni, Ladylike, scripted female-led pilots).

rubrics_metrics.name: fit with network breakout hits/brand
rubrics_metrics.description: looking to build on the success of the network’s breakout hit Awkward. That led to Faking It.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MTV prefers pilots that align with or can extend the tone/appeal of existing successful series — shows that echo what has worked for the network and can become part of its recognizable slate.

rubrics_metrics.name: leveraging existing franchise talent and IP
rubrics_metrics.description: On the unscripted side, where the shift was signaled by moves like spinning of Guy Code into Girl Code, MTV has greenlighted new series Ladylike, which features several Girl Code alums, including Byer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using talent, alumni, or concepts from existing successful franchises (spin-offs, offshoots, ensemble members) is a clear pathway for new series orders; established franchise associations are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: comedic voice and sensibility: smart, candid, norm‑challenging
rubrics_metrics.description: "Girl Code is all about smart and funny women who aren’t afraid to talk about anything, and Ladylike takes that sensibility to the streets to raise hell and challenge a few gender norms along the way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that foreground a bold, candid comedic voice — smart, funny women who challenge social/gender norms — are highlighted as desirable; tone and point-of-view matter as much as premise.

rubrics_metrics.name: distinctive premise or hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ordered project has a distinct conceit: a hidden-camera prank show redefining 'Ladylike'; an Aunt-Nicole-in-the-suburbs family comedy; a pair of girls running a dope-delivery app; a dark half-hour about a vigilante sorority member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network looks for strong, immediately communicable hooks and high‑concept premises that differentiate a pilot (hidden-camera twist, comedic fish-out-of-water, topical gig-economy angle, vigilante/dark-comedy twist). The article lists pilot descriptions as examples of such hooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: star-driven/comedic-vehicle potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Untitled Nicole Byer Project – Nicole Byer portrays a young adult ... Aunt Nicole will offer her own brand of advice ... Nicole Byer will be a consulting producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating vehicles around recognizable comedians or personalities (star vehicles) is a clear development route; the performer’s persona and involvement (e.g., consulting producer) are part of the package.

rubrics_metrics.name: established creators/producers and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Untitled Kaplan/Elfont Pilot – From writing team and executive producers Deborah Kaplan and Harry Elfont. ... Stacey Sher will serve as executive producer and Robinson will co-executive-produce and wrote the pilot. Robinson is repped by CAA, The Gotham Group, and Ryan Goodell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachment of proven writers, showrunners, executive producers and top agencies/representation is presented as noteworthy — signaling industry support and increasing a project's likelihood of being greenlit.

rubrics_metrics.name: format and tonal clarity (half-hour, dark comedy vs. hidden camera)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ladylike ... this hilarious half-hour hidden camera prank show. Little Darlings is a dark half-hour comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The network orders clearly specified formats and tones (half-hour comedies; hidden-camera vs. scripted dark comedy), indicating that well-defined format/tone is part of how projects are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: marketability and identifiable target segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Their dope delivery app is quickly gaining popularity with foodies, celebrities and – the most particular and crucial consumer – hipsters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilots that demonstrate clear audience segments or cultural market hooks (e.g., appeal to foodies, celebrities, hipsters) are framed as having commercial potential; specific, targetable demographics are a selling point.

rubrics_metrics.name: uniqueness/provocative quality to expand slate
rubrics_metrics.description: "These unique and provocative comedies are the perfect way for us to expand our existing slate," said Lefevre, EVP and Head of Scripted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MTV expresses a desire for programming that is 'unique' and 'provocative' — projects that diversify and expand the network's existing offerings rather than duplicate them.
